203	
204	def diff_schema_versions(
205	    conn: sqlite3.Connection,
206	    dataset_name: str,
207	    from_version: int,
208	    to_version: int,
209	    *,
210	    body: bytes = b"",
211	    query_keys: tuple[str, ...] = (),
212	) -> dict:
213	    """Read-only diff of the persisted field definitions of two versions.
214	
215	    ``from`` is the baseline and ``to`` the target. Only the stored field
216	    definitions (name, type, nullable) are compared; field position is not a
217	    difference. Changes are sorted by field name and each carries ``before``
218	    and ``after`` definitions, null on the side where the field does not
219	    exist. ``compatible`` reports whether the target can take over the
220	    baseline's fields: a removal, a type change or a nullable tightening
221	    (nullable -> not nullable) makes it false; additions and nullable
222	    loosening keep it true.
223	
224	    The endpoint takes no parameters: a non-positive version number is a 422
225	    checked before path resolution, while a non-empty request body or any
226	    query parameter is a 422 raised only after the path dataset and both
227	    versions have resolved, so an unknown dataset/version stays a 404
228	    (mirroring the parameterless audit-report endpoint). Nothing is written.
229	    """
230	    if from_version < 1 or to_version < 1:
231	        raise RequestInvalidError(
232	            "Version numbers in the diff path must be positive integers"
233	        )
234	
235	    dataset = require_dataset(conn, dataset_name)
236	    from_row = _require_schema_version(conn, dataset, from_version)
237	    to_row = _require_schema_version(conn, dataset, to_version)
238	
239	    if body.strip():
240	        raise RequestInvalidError(
241	            "The version diff endpoint does not accept a request body"
242	        )
243	    if query_keys:
244	        raise RequestInvalidError(
245	            "The version diff endpoint does not accept query parameters"
246	        )
247	
248	    from_fields = _version_field_definitions(conn, from_row["id"])
249	    to_fields = _version_field_definitions(conn, to_row["id"])
250	
251	    changes: list[dict] = []
252	    compatible = True
253	    for name in sorted(set(from_fields) | set(to_fields)):
254	        before = from_fields.get(name)
255	        after = to_fields.get(name)
256	        if before == after:
257	            continue
258	        if before is None:
259	            changes.append(
260	                {"field": name, "kind": "added", "before": None, "after": after}
261	            )
262	        elif after is None:
263	            changes.append(
264	                {"field": name, "kind": "removed", "before": before, "after": None}
265	            )
266	            compatible = False
267	        else:
268	            changes.append(
269	                {"field": name, "kind": "changed", "before": before, "after": after}
270	            )
271	            if before["type"] != after["type"] or (
272	                before["nullable"] and not after["nullable"]
273	            ):
274	                compatible = False
275	
276	    return {
277	        "from_version": from_row["version"],
278	        "to_version": to_row["version"],
279	        "compatible": compatible,
280	        "changes": changes,
281	    }

292	    version_number: int,
293	    field_name: str,

295	    role: str,
296	) -> tuple[int, int]:

308	        "SELECT id FROM schema_fields WHERE version_id = ? AND name = ?",

319	def create_lineage_link(
320	    conn: sqlite3.Connection,
321	    *,
322	    target_dataset: str,
323	    target_version: int,
324	    target_field: str,
325	    source_dataset: str,
326	    source_version: int,
327	    source_field: str,
328	) -> dict:
329	    target = require_dataset(conn, target_dataset, role="Target dataset")
330	    source = require_dataset(conn, source_dataset, role="Source dataset")
331	
332	    if source["id"] == target["id"]:
333	        raise RequestInvalidError("Source and target datasets must be different")
334	
335	    target_version_id, target_field_id = _require_field(
336	        conn, target, target_version, target_field, role="Target"
337	    )
338	    source_version_id, source_field_id = _require_field(
339	        conn, source, source_version, source_field, role="Source"
340	    )
341	
342	    existing = conn.execute(
343	        "SELECT id FROM lineage_links WHERE target_field_id = ? AND source_field_id = ?",
344	        (target_field_id, source_field_id),
345	    ).fetchone()
346	    if existing is not None:
347	        raise ConflictError(
348	            "This field mapping has already been registered: "
349	            f"'{source_dataset}' v{source_version}.{source_field} -> "
350	            f"'{target_dataset}' v{target_version}.{target_field}"
351	        )
352	
353	    try:
354	        conn.execute(
355	            "INSERT INTO lineage_links ("
356	            "target_dataset_id, target_version_id, target_field_id, "
357	            "source_dataset_id, source_version_id, source_field_id, created_at"
358	            ") VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
359	            (
360	                target["id"],
361	                target_version_id,
362	                target_field_id,
363	                source["id"],
364	                source_version_id,
365	                source_field_id,
366	                utc_now_iso(),
367	            ),
368	        )
369	    except sqlite3.IntegrityError as exc:
370	        raise ConflictError("This field mapping has already been registered") from exc
371	
372	    # The new edge can only extend the impact of fields that reach its source.
373	    _invalidate_impact_cache_for_upstream(
374	        conn, source["name"], source_version, source_field, source_field_id
375	    )
376	
377	    return {
378	        "target_dataset": target["name"],
379	        "target_version": target_version,
380	        "target_field": target_field,
381	        "source": {
382	            "dataset": source["name"],
383	            "version": source_version,
384	            "field": source_field,
385	        },
386	    }

398	        raise NotFoundError(
399	            f"Schema version {version} of dataset '{dataset_name}' does not exist"
400	        )

403	        "SELECT id, name FROM schema_fields WHERE version_id = ? ORDER BY name",

416	        JOIN    schema_fields sf ON sf.id = ll.source_field_id
417	        JOIN    datasets sd ON sd.id = ll.source_dataset_id

449	def _lineage_forward_edges(
450	    conn: sqlite3.Connection,
451	) -> dict[int, list[tuple[int, dict]]]:
452	    """Adjacency of the lineage graph: source field id -> target field refs."""
453	    rows = conn.execute(
454	        """
455	        SELECT  ll.source_field_id AS source_field_id,
456	                ll.target_field_id AS target_field_id,
457	                td.name            AS target_dataset,
458	                tv.version         AS target_version,
459	                tf.name            AS target_field
460	        FROM    lineage_links ll
461	        JOIN    datasets td ON td.id = ll.target_dataset_id
462	        JOIN    schema_versions tv ON tv.id = ll.target_version_id
463	        JOIN    schema_fields tf ON tf.id = ll.target_field_id
464	        """
465	    ).fetchall()
466	    edges: dict[int, list[tuple[int, dict]]] = {}
467	    for row in rows:
468	        ref = {
469	            "dataset": row["target_dataset"],
470	            "version": row["target_version"],
471	            "field": row["target_field"],
472	        }
473	        edges.setdefault(row["source_field_id"], []).append(
474	            (row["target_field_id"], ref)
475	        )
476	    return edges
477	
478	
479	def _compute_impacted(conn: sqlite3.Connection, source_field_id: int) -> list[dict]:
480	    """All fields reachable downstream of the source, deduplicated and sorted.
481	
482	    The source field id is seeded into the visited set, so cycles terminate
483	    and the source itself never appears in the result.
484	    """
485	    edges = _lineage_forward_edges(conn)
486	    visited = {source_field_id}
487	    impacted: dict[tuple[str, int, str], dict] = {}
488	    queue = [source_field_id]
489	    while queue:
490	        current = queue.pop()
491	        for target_field_id, ref in edges.get(current, ()):
492	            if target_field_id in visited:
493	                continue
494	            visited.add(target_field_id)
495	            impacted[(ref["dataset"], ref["version"], ref["field"])] = ref
496	            queue.append(target_field_id)
497	    return [impacted[key] for key in sorted(impacted)]
498

502	) -> list[dict] | None:

505	        "WHERE source_dataset = ? AND source_version = ? AND source_field = ?",
506	        (dataset, version, field),
507	    ).fetchone()

511	def _impact_cache_store(
512	    conn: sqlite3.Connection,
513	    dataset: str,
514	    version: int,
515	    field: str,
516	    impacted: list[dict],
517	) -> None:
518	    conn.execute(
519	        "DELETE FROM lineage_impact_cache "
520	        "WHERE source_dataset = ? AND source_version = ? AND source_field = ?",
521	        (dataset, version, field),
522	    )
523	    cursor = conn.execute(
524	        "INSERT INTO lineage_impact_cache ("
525	        "source_dataset, source_version, source_field, impacted, created_at"
526	        ") VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
527	        (dataset, version, field, json.dumps(impacted), utc_now_iso()),
528	    )
529	    cache_id = cursor.lastrowid
530	    mentioned = {dataset} | {item["dataset"] for item in impacted}
531	    conn.executemany(
532	        "INSERT INTO lineage_impact_cache_datasets (cache_id, dataset) "
533	        "VALUES (?, ?)",
534	        [(cache_id, name) for name in sorted(mentioned)],
535	    )

538	def invalidate_impact_cache_for_dataset(
539	    conn: sqlite3.Connection, dataset_name: str
540	) -> None:
541	    """Drop every cache entry that mentions the dataset in any role."""
542	    conn.execute(

550	def _invalidate_impact_cache_for_upstream(
551	    conn: sqlite3.Connection,
552	    source_dataset: str,
553	    source_version: int,
554	    source_field: str,
555	    source_field_id: int,
556	) -> None:
557	    """Invalidate cached impacts of the new link's source and its upstream.
558	
559	    A new mapping ``source -> target`` only changes the impact result of
560	    fields that can reach ``source`` (``source`` itself included), so exactly
561	    those cached entries are dropped; unrelated entries are kept. The reverse
562	    walk runs after the link was inserted so cycles are covered too.
563	    """
564	    rows = conn.execute(
565	        """
566	        SELECT  ll.target_field_id AS target_field_id,
567	                ll.source_field_id AS source_field_id,
568	                sd.name            AS source_dataset,
569	                sv.version         AS source_version,
570	                sf.name            AS source_field
571	        FROM    lineage_links ll
572	        JOIN    datasets sd ON sd.id = ll.source_dataset_id
573	        JOIN    schema_versions sv ON sv.id = ll.source_version_id
574	        JOIN    schema_fields sf ON sf.id = ll.source_field_id
575	        """
576	    ).fetchall()
577	    reverse: dict[int, list[sqlite3.Row]] = {}
578	    for row in rows:
579	        reverse.setdefault(row["target_field_id"], []).append(row)
580	
581	    visited = {source_field_id}
582	    upstream = {(source_dataset, source_version, source_field)}
583	    queue = [source_field_id]
584	    while queue:
585	        current = queue.pop()
586	        for row in reverse.get(current, ()):
587	            if row["source_field_id"] in visited:
588	                continue
589	            visited.add(row["source_field_id"])
590	            upstream.add(
591	                (row["source_dataset"], row["source_version"], row["source_field"])
592	            )
593	            queue.append(row["source_field_id"])
594	
595	    conn.executemany(
596	        "DELETE FROM lineage_impact_cache "
597	        "WHERE source_dataset = ? AND source_version = ? AND source_field = ?",
598	        sorted(upstream),
599	    )
600	
601	
602	def get_lineage_impact(
603	    conn: sqlite3.Connection, dataset_name: str, version: int, field: str
604	) -> dict:
605	    dataset = require_dataset(conn, dataset_name)
606	    _, field_id = _require_field(conn, dataset, version, field, role="Source")
607	
608	    impacted = _impact_cache_lookup(conn, dataset["name"], version, field)
609	    if impacted is None:
610	        impacted = _compute_impacted(conn, field_id)
611	        _impact_cache_store(conn, dataset["name"], version, field, impacted)
612	
613	    return {
614	        "source": {"dataset": dataset["name"], "version": version, "field": field},
615	        "impacted": impacted,
616	    }

649	def _is_finite_number(value: Any) -> bool:
650	    # bool is a subclass of int; a boolean is not a numeric value here.
651	    if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, (int, float)):
652	        return False
653	    return math.isfinite(value)

656	def _validate_rule_params(
657	    kind: str, params: dict[str, Any], field_names: set[str]
658	) -> None:
659	    """Validate rule parameters structurally (422) and against the schema (404)."""
660	
661	    def require_existing_field(field_name: Any) -> str:
662	        if not isinstance(field_name, str) or not field_name:
663	            raise RequestInvalidError(
664	                f"Rule kind '{kind}' requires a non-empty 'field' parameter"
665	            )
666	        if field_name not in field_names:
667	            raise NotFoundError(f"Field '{field_name}' does not exist in this version")
668	        return field_name
669	
670	    if kind == "not_null":
671	        require_existing_field(params.get("field"))
672	        return
673	
674	    if kind == "numeric_range":
675	        field_name = require_existing_field(params.get("field"))
676	        minimum = params.get("min")
677	        maximum = params.get("max")
678	        if not _is_finite_number(minimum) or not _is_finite_number(maximum):
679	            raise RequestInvalidError(
680	                f"Rule on field '{field_name}' requires finite numeric 'min' and 'max'"
681	            )
682	        if minimum > maximum:
683	            raise RequestInvalidError(
684	                f"Rule on field '{field_name}' requires min <= max"
685	            )
686	        return
687	
688	    if kind == "unique":
689	        fields = params.get("fields")
690	        if not isinstance(fields, list) or not fields:
691	            raise RequestInvalidError(
692	                "Rule kind 'unique' requires a non-empty 'fields' list"
693	            )
694	        if not all(isinstance(name, str) and name for name in fields):
695	            raise RequestInvalidError(
696	                "Rule kind 'unique' requires 'fields' to contain non-empty field names"
697	            )
698	        if len(set(fields)) != len(fields):
699	            raise RequestInvalidError(
700	                "Rule kind 'unique' requires 'fields' to contain no duplicates"
701	            )
702	        unknown = [name for name in fields if name not in field_names]
703	        if unknown:
704	            raise NotFoundError(
705	                f"Field '{unknown[0]}' does not exist in this version"
706	            )
707	        return

809	def _row_violates_not_null(row: dict[str, Any], field: str) -> bool:
810	    return field not in row or row[field] is None
811	
812	
813	def _row_violates_numeric_range(
814	    row: dict[str, Any], field: str, minimum: float, maximum: float
815	) -> bool:
816	    if field not in row:
817	        return True
818	    value = row[field]
819	    if value is None or not _is_finite_number(value):
820	        return True
821	    return value < minimum or value > maximum
822	
823	
824	def _row_violates_unique(row: dict[str, Any], fields: list[str]) -> tuple:
825	    return tuple(None if name not in row else row[name] for name in fields)
826	
827	
828	def _json_combo_key(combo: tuple) -> str:
829	    # Values are already JSON-decoded scalars (or nested arrays/objects); use
830	    # JSON text so that, e.g., the number 1 and the string "1" never compare
831	    # equal and nested objects with reordered keys still match.
832	    return json.dumps(combo, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"))
833

835	def evaluate_quality_rules(
836	    conn: sqlite3.Connection, dataset_name: str, version_number: int, rows: list[dict]
837	) -> dict:
838	    dataset = require_dataset(conn, dataset_name)
839	    version_row = _require_schema_version(conn, dataset, version_number)
840	
841	    rule_rows = conn.execute(
842	        "SELECT id, name, kind, params, enabled "
843	        "FROM quality_rules WHERE version_id = ? AND enabled = 1 ORDER BY id",
844	        (version_row["id"],),
845	    ).fetchall()
846	
847	    results: list[dict] = []
848	    for rule_row in rule_rows:
849	        params = json.loads(rule_row["params"])
850	        kind = rule_row["kind"]
851	        violations: list[int] = []
852	
853	        if kind == "not_null":
854	            field = params["field"]
855	            violations = [
856	                index
857	                for index, row in enumerate(rows)
858	                if _row_violates_not_null(row, field)
859	            ]
860	        elif kind == "numeric_range":
861	            field = params["field"]
862	            violations = [
863	                index
864	                for index, row in enumerate(rows)
865	                if _row_violates_numeric_range(
866	                    row, field, params["min"], params["max"]
867	                )
868	            ]
869	        elif kind == "unique":
870	            fields = params["fields"]
871	            seen: dict[str, int] = {}
872	            duplicated: set[int] = set()
873	            for index, row in enumerate(rows):
874	                combo = _row_violates_unique(row, fields)
875	                key = _json_combo_key(combo)
876	                if key in seen:
877	                    duplicated.add(seen[key])
878	                    duplicated.add(index)
879	                else:
880	                    seen[key] = index
881	            violations = sorted(duplicated)
882	
883	        results.append(
884	            {
885	                "rule_id": rule_row["id"],
886	                "name": rule_row["name"],
887	                "passed": not violations,
888	                "violations": violations,
889	            }
890	        )
891	
892	    return {
893	        "dataset": dataset["name"],
894	        "version": version_row["version"],
895	        "results": results,
896	    }

1171	def _parse_at_timestamp(raw: str) -> datetime:
1172	    try:
1173	        parsed = datetime.fromisoformat(raw)
1174	    except (TypeError, ValueError) as exc:
1175	        raise RequestInvalidError(
1176	            "Query parameter 'timestamp' must be an ISO-8601 date-time"
1177	        ) from exc
1178	    # A trailing timezone designator (offset or 'Z') is mandatory.
1179	    if parsed.tzinfo is None or parsed.utcoffset() is None:
1180	        raise RequestInvalidError(
1181	            "Query parameter 'timestamp' must include a timezone"
1182	        )
1183	    return parsed

1186	def get_snapshot_at(
1187	    conn: sqlite3.Connection,
1188	    dataset_name: str,
1189	    version_number: int,
1190	    raw_timestamp: str | None,
1191	) -> dict:
1192	    if raw_timestamp is None or not raw_timestamp:
1193	        raise RequestInvalidError(
1194	            "Query parameter 'timestamp' is required and must be an ISO-8601 date-time"
1195	        )
1196	    target = _parse_at_timestamp(raw_timestamp)
1197	
1198	    dataset = require_dataset(conn, dataset_name)
1199	    version_row = _require_schema_version(conn, dataset, version_number)
1200	
1201	    # Select the newest snapshot chronologically (ties broken by the highest
1202	    # id); comparing parsed instants also handles any offset in the target.
1203	    candidates = conn.execute(
1204	        "SELECT id, created_at FROM snapshots WHERE version_id = ?",
1205	        (version_row["id"],),
1206	    ).fetchall()
1207	    eligible = [
1208	        (datetime.fromisoformat(row["created_at"]), row["id"])
1209	        for row in candidates
1210	        if datetime.fromisoformat(row["created_at"]) <= target
1211	    ]
1212	    if not eligible:
1213	        raise NotFoundError(
1214	            f"No snapshot of version {version_number} of dataset "
1215	            f"'{dataset_name}' exists at or before the requested timestamp"
1216	        )
1217	    match_id = max(eligible, key=lambda item: (item[0], item[1]))[1]
1218	
1219	    row = conn.execute(
1220	        "SELECT id, row_count, rows, created_at FROM snapshots WHERE id = ?",
1221	        (match_id,),
1222	    ).fetchone()
1223	    result = _snapshot_metadata(row, dataset["name"], version_row["version"])
1224	    result["rows"] = json.loads(row["rows"])
1225	    return result

1252	    rows: list[dict[str, Any]],
1253	) -> tuple[Counter, dict[str, dict[str, Any]]]:
1254	    counts: Counter = Counter()
1255	    examples: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}

1258	        counts[key] += 1

1263	def diff_snapshots(
1264	    conn: sqlite3.Connection,
1265	    dataset_name: str,
1266	    version_number: int,
1267	    from_snapshot_id: int,
1268	    to_snapshot_id: int,
1269	) -> dict:
1270	    # Validate the path target first so unknown dataset/version stay 404.
1271	    dataset = require_dataset(conn, dataset_name)
1272	    version_row = _require_schema_version(conn, dataset, version_number)
1273	
1274	    from_row = _find_snapshot_globally(conn, from_snapshot_id)
1275	    if from_row is None:
1276	        raise NotFoundError(f"Snapshot {from_snapshot_id} does not exist")
1277	    to_row = _find_snapshot_globally(conn, to_snapshot_id)
1278	    if to_row is None:
1279	        raise NotFoundError(f"Snapshot {to_snapshot_id} does not exist")
1280	
1281	    for row, snapshot_id in ((from_row, from_snapshot_id), (to_row, to_snapshot_id)):
1282	        if row["version_id"] != version_row["id"]:
1283	            raise RequestInvalidError(
1284	                f"Snapshot {snapshot_id} does not belong to version "
1285	                f"{version_number} of dataset '{dataset_name}'; snapshots can "
1286	                "only be compared within the same dataset and version"
1287	            )
1288	
1289	    from_rows = json.loads(from_row["rows"])
1290	    to_rows = json.loads(to_row["rows"])
1291	    from_counts, from_examples = _snapshot_multiset(from_rows)
1292	    to_counts, to_examples = _snapshot_multiset(to_rows)
1293	
1294	    added_keys = sorted(key for key in to_counts if to_counts[key] > from_counts[key])
1295	    removed_keys = sorted(key for key in from_counts if from_counts[key] > to_counts[key])
1296	
1297	    return {
1298	        "from_snapshot_id": from_snapshot_id,
1299	        "to_snapshot_id": to_snapshot_id,
1300	        "added": [
1301	            {"row": to_examples[key], "count": to_counts[key] - from_counts[key]}
1302	            for key in added_keys
1303	        ],
1304	        "removed": [
1305	            {"row": from_examples[key], "count": from_counts[key] - to_counts[key]}
1306	            for key in removed_keys
1307	        ],
1308	    }

1356	def _compute_version_field_impacted(
1357	    conn: sqlite3.Connection, version_id: int
1358	) -> list[dict]:
1359	    """Downstream union of every field of one schema version.
1360	
1361	    All of the version's fields seed the same reachability walk, so direct and
1362	    indirect downstream fields are found once, cycles terminate and the version's
1363	    own fields never appear in the result.
1364	    """
1365	    field_rows = conn.execute(
1366	        "SELECT id FROM schema_fields WHERE version_id = ?", (version_id,)
1367	    ).fetchall()
1368	    seeds = [row["id"] for row in field_rows]
1369	
1370	    edges = _lineage_forward_edges(conn)
1371	    visited = set(seeds)
1372	    impacted: dict[tuple[str, int, str], dict] = {}
1373	    queue = list(seeds)
1374	    while queue:
1375	        current = queue.pop()
1376	        for target_field_id, ref in edges.get(current, ()):
1377	            if target_field_id in visited:
1378	                continue
1379	            visited.add(target_field_id)
1380	            impacted[(ref["dataset"], ref["version"], ref["field"])] = ref
1381	            queue.append(target_field_id)
1382	    return [impacted[key] for key in sorted(impacted)]
1383

1397	def create_snapshot_deletion_request(
1398	    conn: sqlite3.Connection,
1399	    dataset_name: str,
1400	    version_number: int,
1401	    snapshot_id: int,
1402	    reason: str,
1403	) -> dict:
1404	    dataset = require_dataset(conn, dataset_name)
1405	    version_row = _require_schema_version(conn, dataset, version_number)
1406	
1407	    clean_reason = reason.strip()
1408	    if not clean_reason:
1409	        raise RequestInvalidError("'reason' must not be empty")
1410	
1411	    snapshot_row = _get_scoped_snapshot_row(conn, version_row["id"], snapshot_id)
1412	    if snapshot_row is None:
1413	        raise NotFoundError(
1414	            f"Snapshot {snapshot_id} does not exist in version "
1415	            f"{version_number} of dataset '{dataset_name}'"
1416	        )
1417	
1418	    policy_row = conn.execute(
1419	        "SELECT id FROM retention_policies WHERE version_id = ?",
1420	        (version_row["id"],),
1421	    ).fetchone()
1422	    if policy_row is None:
1423	        raise NotFoundError(
1424	            f"No retention policy exists for version {version_number} of "
1425	            f"dataset '{dataset_name}'"
1426	        )
1427	
1428	    open_request = conn.execute(
1429	        "SELECT id FROM snapshot_deletion_requests "
1430	        "WHERE snapshot_id = ? AND status IN ('pending', 'blocked')",
1431	        (snapshot_id,),
1432	    ).fetchone()
1433	    if open_request is not None:
1434	        raise ConflictError(
1435	            f"Snapshot {snapshot_id} already has an open deletion request "
1436	            f"({open_request['id']})"
1437	        )
1438	
1439	    # An active retention exception (version- or snapshot-scoped) forbids
1440	    # opening a deletion request; the check shares this transaction with the
1441	    # insert below, so the two commit atomically.
1442	    _require_no_active_retention_exception(
1443	        conn, version_row, snapshot_id, dataset_name, version_number
1444	    )
1445	
1446	    impacted = _compute_version_field_impacted(conn, version_row["id"])
1447	    status = "blocked" if impacted else "pending"
1448	    try:
1449	        cursor = conn.execute(
1450	            "INSERT INTO snapshot_deletion_requests ("
1451	            "version_id, snapshot_id, policy_id, reason, status, impacted, created_at"
1452	            ") VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
1453	            (
1454	                version_row["id"],
1455	                snapshot_id,
1456	                policy_row["id"],
1457	                clean_reason,
1458	                status,
1459	                json.dumps(impacted),
1460	                utc_now_iso(),
1461	            ),
1462	        )
1463	    except sqlite3.IntegrityError as exc:
1464	        # Lost a race against a concurrent open-request insert.
1465	        raise ConflictError(
1466	            f"Snapshot {snapshot_id} already has an open deletion request"
1467	        ) from exc
1468	    row = conn.execute(
1469	        "SELECT * FROM snapshot_deletion_requests WHERE id = ?",
1470	        (cursor.lastrowid,),
1471	    ).fetchone()
1472	    return _deletion_request_row_to_dict(row)

1475	def list_snapshot_deletion_requests(
1476	    conn: sqlite3.Connection,
1477	    dataset_name: str,
1478	    version_number: int,
1479	    snapshot_id: int,
1480	) -> list[dict]:
1481	    dataset = require_dataset(conn, dataset_name)
1482	    version_row = _require_schema_version(conn, dataset, version_number)
1483	
1484	    # The collection stays addressable after its snapshot has been confirmed
1485	    # away: the snapshot itself may be gone, but its request records remain.
1486	    # A snapshot id that never existed in this version and has no requests is an
1487	    # unknown resource.
1488	    snapshot_row = _get_scoped_snapshot_row(conn, version_row["id"], snapshot_id)
1489	    request_rows = conn.execute(
1490	        "SELECT id FROM snapshot_deletion_requests "
1491	        "WHERE version_id = ? AND snapshot_id = ?",
1492	        (version_row["id"], snapshot_id),
1493	    ).fetchall()
1494	    if snapshot_row is None and not request_rows:
1495	        raise NotFoundError(
1496	            f"Snapshot {snapshot_id} does not exist in version "
1497	            f"{version_number} of dataset '{dataset_name}'"
1498	        )
1499	
1500	    rows = conn.execute(
1501	        "SELECT * FROM snapshot_deletion_requests "

2288	def _graph_reaches_target(
2289	    graph: dict[int, list[int]], start: int, target: int
2290	) -> bool:
2291	    """Whether ``target`` is reachable from ``start`` along dependency edges."""
2292	    visited = {start}
2293	    stack = [start]
2294	    while stack:
2295	        current = stack.pop()
2296	        for dependency in graph.get(current, ()):
2297	            if dependency == target:
2298	                return True
2299	            if dependency not in visited:
2300	                visited.add(dependency)
2301	                stack.append(dependency)
2302	    return False

2305	def replace_task_dependencies(
2306	    conn: sqlite3.Connection,
2307	    dataset_name: str,
2308	    version_number: int,
2309	    task_id: int,
2310	    depends_on: list[int],
2311	) -> dict:
2312	    dataset = require_dataset(conn, dataset_name)
2313	    version_row = _require_schema_version(conn, dataset, version_number)
2314	    task_row = _require_task(
2315	        conn, version_row, dataset_name, version_number, task_id
2316	    )
2317	
2318	    if len(set(depends_on)) != len(depends_on):
2319	        raise RequestInvalidError("'depends_on' must not contain duplicate task ids")
2320	    if task_id in depends_on:
2321	        raise ConflictError(
2322	            f"Processing task {task_id} must not depend on itself"
2323	        )
2324	
2325	    task_rows = _version_task_rows(conn, version_row["id"])
2326	    existing_ids = {row["id"] for row in task_rows}
2327	    unknown = [dependency_id for dependency_id in depends_on if dependency_id not in existing_ids]
2328	    if unknown:
2329	        raise NotFoundError(
2330	            f"Dependency task {unknown[0]} does not exist in version "
2331	            f"{version_number} of dataset '{dataset_name}'"
2332	        )
2333	
2334	    if task_row["status"] != "pending":
2335	        raise ConflictError(
2336	            f"Processing task {task_id} is '{task_row['status']}'; only pending "
2337	            "tasks can have their dependencies replaced"
2338	        )
2339	
2340	    # Build the prospective graph (the target task's edges replaced, every other
2341	    # task unchanged) and reject cycles. Only the target's edges change, so any
2342	    # newly introduced cycle must pass through the target: it exists iff a new
2343	    # dependency can already reach the target.
2344	    graph = _task_dependency_graph(task_rows)
2345	    graph[task_row["id"]] = list(depends_on)
2346	    if any(
2347	        _graph_reaches_target(graph, dependency_id, task_row["id"])
2348	        for dependency_id in depends_on
2349	    ):
2350	        raise ConflictError(
2351	            "Replacing the dependencies would introduce a cycle in the task graph"
2352	        )
2353	
2354	    # Validation above shares this transaction with the write, so the replacement
2355	    # either commits atomically or leaves the graph untouched.
2356	    conn.execute(
2357	        "UPDATE processing_tasks SET depends_on = ? WHERE id = ?",
2358	        (json.dumps(list(depends_on)), task_row["id"]),
2359	    )
2360	    updated = conn.execute(
2361	        "SELECT * FROM processing_tasks WHERE id = ?", (task_row["id"],)
2362	    ).fetchone()
2363	    return _task_row_to_dict(updated, dataset["name"], version_row["version"])

2366	def _schedule_states(
2367	    graph: dict[int, tuple[str, int, int, list[int]]],
2368	) -> dict[int, str]:
2369	    """Derive the schedule state of every task in one version.
2370	
2371	    Non-pending tasks map directly from their stored status (``failed`` splits
2372	    into ``retryable``/``exhausted`` on remaining attempts). Pending tasks are
2373	    resolved against their dependencies by fixed-point propagation: all direct
2374	    dependencies succeeded -> ``ready``; any dependency chain exhausted or
2375	    already ``upstream_failed`` -> ``upstream_failed``; otherwise ``blocked``.
2376	    The graph is acyclic (enforced at creation and on every replacement), so
2377	    the propagation terminates.
2378	    """
2379	    states: dict[int, str] = {}
2380	    for task_id, (status, attempt_count, max_attempts, _deps) in graph.items():
2381	        if status == "pending":
2382	            continue
2383	        if status == "failed":
2384	            states[task_id] = (
2385	                "retryable" if attempt_count < max_attempts else "exhausted"
2386	            )
2387	        else:
2388	            states[task_id] = status
2389	
2390	    changed = True
2391	    while changed:
2392	        changed = False
2393	        for task_id, (status, _attempt_count, _max_attempts, deps) in graph.items():
2394	            if status != "pending":
2395	                continue
2396	            if any(
2397	                states.get(dependency_id) in ("exhausted", "upstream_failed")
2398	                for dependency_id in deps
2399	            ):
2400	                new_state = "upstream_failed"
2401	            elif all(
2402	                states.get(dependency_id) == "succeeded" for dependency_id in deps
2403	            ):
2404	                # An empty dependency list vacuously satisfies "all succeeded".
2405	                new_state = "ready"
2406	            else:
2407	                new_state = "blocked"
2408	            if states.get(task_id) != new_state:
2409	                states[task_id] = new_state
2410	                changed = True
2411	    return states

2414	def get_processing_schedule(
2415	    conn: sqlite3.Connection, dataset_name: str, version_number: int
2416	) -> dict:
2417	    dataset = require_dataset(conn, dataset_name)
2418	    version_row = _require_schema_version(conn, dataset, version_number)
2419	
2420	    rows = _version_task_rows(conn, version_row["id"])
2421	    graph: dict[int, tuple[str, int, int, list[int]]] = {
2422	        row["id"]: (
2423	            row["status"],
2424	            row["attempt_count"],
2425	            row["max_attempts"],
2426	            json.loads(row["depends_on"]),
2427	        )
2428	        for row in rows
2429	    }
2430	    states = _schedule_states(graph)

2461	# is the hard guard against writers in other processes; such a collision is
2462	# resolved with a bounded re-read-and-retry.
2463	_audit_append_locks: dict[int, threading.Lock] = {}

2466	# Bound on re-read-and-retry attempts when a writer in another process wins the
2467	# race for the same (run_id, sequence).

2472	    with _audit_append_locks_guard:
2473	        lock = _audit_append_locks.get(run_id)
2474	        if lock is None:
2475	            lock = threading.Lock()
2476	            _audit_append_locks[run_id] = lock
2477	        return lock

2490	def _audit_evidence_hash(record: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
2491	    """SHA-256 over the canonical JSON of every hashed field.
2492	
2493	    Keys are sorted by Unicode code point, no whitespace is emitted and the
2494	    text is UTF-8 encoded (non-ASCII characters are not escaped). ``id``,
2495	    ``created_at`` and ``evidence_hash`` itself are excluded.
2496	    """
2497	    payload = {field: record[field] for field in AUDIT_EVIDENCE_FIELDS}
2498	    canonical = json.dumps(
2499	        payload, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False
2500	    )
2501	    return hashlib.sha256(canonical.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()

2548	def create_audit_record(
2549	    conn: sqlite3.Connection,
2550	    dataset_name: str,
2551	    version_number: int,
2552	    task_id: int,
2553	    run_id: int,
2554	    event: str,
2555	    input_summary: str,
2556	    result_summary: str,
2557	) -> dict:
2558	    # Precedence mirrors finishing a run: the path dataset/version/task must
2559	    # exist (404); blank fields are then rejected (422); finally the run itself
2560	    # must exist (404) and belong to the path task (422).
2561	    dataset = require_dataset(conn, dataset_name)
2562	    version_row = _require_schema_version(conn, dataset, version_number)
2563	    task_row = _require_task(
2564	        conn, version_row, dataset_name, version_number, task_id
2565	    )
2566	
2567	    for label, value in (
2568	        ("event", event),
2569	        ("input_summary", input_summary),
2570	        ("result_summary", result_summary),
2571	    ):
2572	        if not value.strip():
2573	            raise RequestInvalidError(f"'{label}' must not be empty")
2574	
2575	    run_row = conn.execute(
2576	        "SELECT * FROM processing_task_runs WHERE id = ?", (run_id,)
2577	    ).fetchone()
2578	    if run_row is None:
2579	        raise NotFoundError(f"Processing task run {run_id} does not exist")
2580	    if run_row["task_id"] != task_row["id"]:
2581	        raise RequestInvalidError(
2582	            f"Processing task run {run_id} does not belong to task {task_id} "
2583	            f"in version {version_number} of dataset '{dataset_name}'"
2584	        )
2585	
2586	    # The per-run lock makes read-tail -> append atomic within this process
2587	    # (FastAPI runs this synchronous endpoint in one process's threadpool).
2588	    # The UNIQUE(run_id, sequence) constraint is the hard cross-process guard;
2589	    # a writer that loses a race against another process retries with the new
2590	    # tail instead of failing the request.
2591	    with _audit_append_lock(run_id):
2592	        for attempt in range(_AUDIT_APPEND_MAX_ATTEMPTS):
2593	            # Read the run status and chain tail immediately before inserting so
2594	            # both reflect the state at write time.
2595	            run_status = conn.execute(
2596	                "SELECT status FROM processing_task_runs WHERE id = ?", (run_id,)
2597	            ).fetchone()["status"]

2599	                "SELECT sequence, evidence_hash FROM processing_task_audit_records "
2600	                "WHERE run_id = ? ORDER BY sequence DESC LIMIT 1",
2601	                (run_id,),

2603	            if tail is None:
2604	                sequence = 1
2605	                previous_hash = None
2606	            else:
2607	                sequence = tail["sequence"] + 1
2608	                previous_hash = tail["evidence_hash"]
2609	
2610	            record = {
2611	                "sequence": sequence,
2612	                "event": event,
2613	                "input_summary": input_summary,
2614	                "result_summary": result_summary,
2615	                "run_status": run_status,
2616	                "previous_hash": previous_hash,
2617	            }
2618	            try:
2619	                cursor = conn.execute(
2620	                    "INSERT INTO processing_task_audit_records ("
2621	                    "run_id, sequence, event, input_summary, result_summary, "
2622	                    "run_status, previous_hash, evidence_hash, created_at"
2623	                    ") VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
2624	                    (
2625	                        run_id,
2626	                        sequence,
2627	                        event,

                       REFERENCES schema_versions(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
        retention_days INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (retention_days >= 0),
        created_at     TEXT NOT NULL
    )
    """,
    # A confirmed request must survive the deletion of its snapshot, so the
    # snapshot link is intentionally a plain integer instead of a cascading
    # foreign key (snapshots are only deleted through a confirmed request).
    """
    CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS snapshot_deletion_requests (
        id           INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
        version_id   INTEGER NOT NULL,
        snapshot_id  INTEGER NOT NULL,
        policy_id    INTEGER NOT NULL
                     REFERENCES retention_policies(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
        reason       TEXT NOT NULL,
        status       TEXT NOT NULL
                     CHECK (status IN ('pending', 'blocked', 'confirmed')),
        impacted     TEXT NOT NULL,
        created_at   TEXT NOT NULL,
        confirmed_at TEXT
    )
    """,
    # At most one open (pending/blocked) request per snapshot; confirmed
    # requests never block a new request once the snapshot is deleted.
    """
    CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS
        idx_snapshot_deletion_requests_one_open
    ON snapshot_deletion_requests (snapshot_id)
    WHERE status IN ('pending', 'blocked')
    """,
    # A released or expired exception must survive the deletion of the snapshot
    # it named, so the snapshot link is intentionally a plain integer instead of
    # a cascading foreign key (mirroring snapshot_deletion_requests).
    """
    CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS retention_exceptions (
        id          INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
        version_id  INTEGER NOT NULL
                    REFERENCES schema_versions(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
        scope       TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (scope IN ('version', 'snapshot')),
        snapshot_id INTEGER,
        reason      TEXT NOT NULL,
        expires_at  TEXT NOT NULL,
        status      TEXT NOT NULL
                    CHECK (status IN ('active', 'released')),
        created_at  TEXT NOT NULL,
        released_at TEXT,
        CHECK (
            (scope = 'version' AND snapshot_id IS NULL) OR
            (scope = 'snapshot' AND snapshot_id IS NOT NULL)
        )
    )
    """,
    # Persistent cache of field-impact query results, keyed by the source
    # field. Entries are invalidated whenever a committed write could change
    # what is reachable from the cached source (see app.repository).
    """
    CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS lineage_impact_cache (
        id             INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
        source_dataset TEXT NOT NULL,
        source_version INTEGER NOT NULL,
        source_field   TEXT NOT NULL,
        impacted       TEXT NOT NULL,
        created_at     TEXT NOT NULL,
        UNIQUE (source_dataset, source_version, source_field)
    )
    """,
    # Datasets mentioned by each cache entry (as source or inside the impacted
    # result) so that per-dataset invalidation stays a simple indexed delete.
    """
    CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS lineage_impact_cache_datasets (
        cache_id INTEGER NOT NULL
                 REFERENCES lineage_impact_cache(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
        dataset  TEXT NOT NULL
    )
    """,
    # Audit records are an append-only proof chain: the database itself refuses
    # updates and deletes so the evidence history cannot be rewritten.
    """
    CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS trg_processing_audit_records_no_update
    BEFORE UPDATE ON processing_task_audit_records
    BEGIN
        SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'processing task audit records are immutable');
    END
    """,
    """
    CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS trg_processing_audit_records_no_delete
    BEFORE DELETE ON processing_task_audit_records
    BEGIN
        SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'processing task audit records are immutable');
    END
    """,
)


def database_path() -> Path:
    return Path(os.environ.get("DATA_LINEAGE_DB", DEFAULT_DB_PATH))


def _connect() -> sqlite3.Connection:
    path = database_path()
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    conn = sqlite3.connect(path, timeout=30)
    conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
    conn.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON")
    # Schema creation is idempotent and committed independently, so every
    # request works against an initialized database file.
    for statement in SCHEMA_STATEMENTS:
        conn.execute(statement)
    conn.commit()
    return conn


@contextmanager
def db_session() -> Iterator[sqlite3.Connection]:
    conn = _connect()
    try:
        yield conn
        conn.commit()
    except BaseException:
        conn.rollback()
        raise
    finally:
        conn.close()


def get_db() -> Iterator[sqlite3.Connection]:
    """FastAPI dependency yielding a transactional database connection."""
    with db_session() as conn:
        yield conn

"""Tests for cancelling a running processing-task run.

POST .../processing-tasks/{task_id}/runs/{run_id}/cancel
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
import subprocess
import sys
import threading
from datetime import datetime
from pathlib import Path

from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

PROJECT_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]

TASKS_PATH = "/datasets/orders/versions/1/processing-tasks"
DISPATCH_PATH = f"{TASKS_PATH}/dispatch"

RUN_FIELDS = {
    "id",
    "task_id",
    "attempt",
    "status",
    "started_at",
    "finished_at",
    "error",
}


def create_dataset_and_version(client: TestClient, dataset: str = "orders") -> None:
    response = client.post("/datasets", json={"name": dataset})
    assert response.status_code == 201, response.text
    response = client.post(
        f"/datasets/{dataset}/versions",
        json={"fields": [{"name": "id", "type": "integer", "nullable": False}]},
    )
    assert response.status_code == 201, response.text


def make_task(client: TestClient, name: str, **overrides) -> dict:
    response = client.post(TASKS_PATH, json={"name": name, **overrides})
    assert response.status_code == 201, response.text
    return response.json()


def run_task(client: TestClient, task_id: int) -> dict:
    response = client.post(f"{TASKS_PATH}/{task_id}/runs")
    assert response.status_code == 201, response.text
    return response.json()


def task_detail(client: TestClient, task_id: int) -> dict:
    response = client.get(f"{TASKS_PATH}/{task_id}")
    assert response.status_code == 200, response.text
    return response.json()


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Successful cancellation
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #


def test_cancel_running_run_marks_run_and_task_failed(client: TestClient) -> None:
    create_dataset_and_version(client)
    task = make_task(client, "ingest", max_attempts=3)
    run = run_task(client, task["id"])

    response = client.post(
        f"{TASKS_PATH}/{task['id']}/runs/{run['id']}/cancel",
        json={"reason": "operator abort"},
    )
    assert response.status_code == 200, response.text
    body = response.json()
    assert set(body) == RUN_FIELDS
    assert body["id"] == run["id"]
    assert body["task_id"] == task["id"]
    assert body["attempt"] == 1
    assert body["status"] == "failed"
    assert body["error"] == "operator abort"
    assert body["finished_at"] is not None
    datetime.fromisoformat(body["finished_at"])
    assert datetime.fromisoformat(body["finished_at"]) >= datetime.fromisoformat(
        body["started_at"]
    )

    detail = task_detail(client, task["id"])
    # The task is failed but the consumed attempt is not rolled back.
    assert detail["status"] == "failed"
    assert detail["attempt_count"] == 1
    assert len(detail["runs"]) == 1
    assert detail["runs"][0]["status"] == "failed"
    assert detail["runs"][0]["finished_at"] == body["finished_at"]


def test_cancel_trims_reason_before_storing(client: TestClient) -> None:
    create_dataset_and_version(client)
    task = make_task(client, "ingest")
    run = run_task(client, task["id"])
    response = client.post(
        f"{TASKS_PATH}/{task['id']}/runs/{run['id']}/cancel",
        json={"reason": "  stop it now \t"},
    )
    assert response.status_code == 200, response.text
    assert response.json()["error"] == "stop it now"


def test_canceled_task_can_start_again_with_continuous_attempts(
    client: TestClient,
) -> None:
    create_dataset_and_version(client)
    task = make_task(client, "flaky", max_attempts=3)

    first = run_task(client, task["id"])
    assert first["attempt"] == 1
    response = client.post(
        f"{TASKS_PATH}/{task['id']}/runs/{first['id']}/cancel",
        json={"reason": "cancel 1"},
    )
    assert response.status_code == 200

    second = run_task(client, task["id"])
    assert second["attempt"] == 2
    response = client.post(
        f"{TASKS_PATH}/{task['id']}/runs/{second['id']}/cancel",
        json={"reason": "cancel 2"},
    )
    assert response.status_code == 200
    detail = task_detail(client, task["id"])
    assert detail["status"] == "failed"
    assert detail["attempt_count"] == 2

    # The last remaining attempt is still handed out continuously.
    third = run_task(client, task["id"])
    assert third["attempt"] == 3
    response = client.post(
        f"{TASKS_PATH}/{task['id']}/runs/{third['id']}/cancel",
        json={"reason": "cancel 3"},
    )
    assert response.status_code == 200

    # Cancelling the final attempt exhausts the task: no further run starts.
    response = client.post(f"{TASKS_PATH}/{task['id']}/runs")
    assert response.status_code == 409
    assert response.json()["error"] == "conflict"
    # No duplicate or skipped attempt numbers were introduced.
    detail = task_detail(client, task["id"])
    assert detail["status"] == "failed"
    assert detail["attempt_count"] == 3
    assert [run["attempt"] for run in detail["runs"]] == [1, 2, 3]


def test_canceled_run_is_selectable_by_dispatch_when_attempts_remain(
    client: TestClient,
) -> None:
    create_dataset_and_version(client)
    task = make_task(client, "flaky", max_attempts=2)
    run = run_task(client, task["id"])
    response = client.post(
        f"{TASKS_PATH}/{task['id']}/runs/{run['id']}/cancel",
        json={"reason": "stop"},
    )
    assert response.status_code == 200

    response = client.post(DISPATCH_PATH, json={"limit": 5})
    assert response.status_code == 201, response.text
    runs = response.json()["runs"]
    assert len(runs) == 1
    assert runs[0]["task_id"] == task["id"]

def test_concurrent_cancel_and_finish_have_single_winner(client: TestClient) -> None:
    create_dataset_and_version(client)
    task = make_task(client, "ingest", max_attempts=3)
    run = run_task(client, task["id"])
    url = f"{TASKS_PATH}/{task['id']}/runs/{run['id']}"

    thread_count = 8
    barrier = threading.Barrier(thread_count)
    results: list[tuple[str, int, dict]] = []
    results_lock = threading.Lock()

    def worker(cancel: bool) -> None:
        thread_client = TestClient(client.app)
        barrier.wait()
        if cancel:
            response = thread_client.post(
                f"{url}/cancel", json={"reason": "operator abort"}
            )
            kind = "cancel"
        else:
            response = thread_client.patch(
                url, json={"status": "succeeded"}
            )
            kind = "finish"
        with results_lock:
            results.append((kind, response.status_code, response.json()))

    threads = [
        threading.Thread(target=worker, args=(index % 2 == 0,))
        for index in range(thread_count)
    ]
    for thread in threads:
        thread.start()
    for thread in threads:
        thread.join()

    successes = [result for result in results if result[1] == 200]
    assert len(successes) == 1, results
    assert all(
        status_code == 409 for _kind, status_code, _body in results if status_code != 200
    )

    # The stored end state is exactly the single committed transition.
    detail = task_detail(client, task["id"])
    stored_run = detail["runs"][0]
    winner_kind, _status, winner_body = successes[0]
    assert stored_run["status"] == winner_body["status"]
    assert stored_run["finished_at"] == winner_body["finished_at"]
    assert stored_run["error"] == winner_body["error"]
    assert stored_run["status"] in ("succeeded", "failed")
    assert stored_run["finished_at"] is not None
    if winner_kind == "cancel":
        assert stored_run["status"] == "failed"
        assert stored_run["error"] == "operator abort"
    else:
        assert stored_run["status"] == "succeeded"
        assert stored_run["error"] is None
    assert detail["status"] == stored_run["status"]
    # No extra runs were created by the racing requests.
    assert len(detail["runs"]) == 1
    assert detail["attempt_count"] == 1


def test_concurrent_cancel_and_starts_keep_one_running_run(client: TestClient) -> None:
    create_dataset_and_version(client)
    task = make_task(client, "flaky", max_attempts=5)
    first = run_task(client, task["id"])
    cancel_url = f"{TASKS_PATH}/{task['id']}/runs/{first['id']}/cancel"
    start_url = f"{TASKS_PATH}/{task['id']}/runs"

    thread_count = 6
    barrier = threading.Barrier(thread_count)
    errors: list[AssertionError] = []

    def worker(is_canceller: bool) -> None:
        thread_client = TestClient(client.app)
        barrier.wait()
        try:
            if is_canceller:
                response = thread_client.post(cancel_url, json={"reason": "stop"})
                assert response.status_code in (200, 409), response.text
                return
            for _ in range(100):
                response = thread_client.post(start_url)
                assert response.status_code in (201, 409), response.text
                if response.status_code == 201:
                    started = response.json()
                    # A started run is itself canceled so the task becomes
                    # retryable again and attempts keep advancing.
                    response = thread_client.post(
                        f"{TASKS_PATH}/{task['id']}/runs/{started['id']}/cancel",
                        json={"reason": "stop"},
                    )
                    assert response.status_code in (200, 409), response.text
        except AssertionError as exc:  # pragma: no cover - reported below
            errors.append(exc)

    threads = [
        threading.Thread(target=worker, args=(index == 0,))
        for index in range(thread_count)
    ]
    for thread in threads:
        thread.start()
    for thread in threads:
        thread.join()
    assert not errors

    detail = task_detail(client, task["id"])
    attempts = [run["attempt"] for run in detail["runs"]]
    # Continuous numbering, no duplicates or gaps and never past the budget.
    assert attempts == list(range(1, len(attempts) + 1))
    assert len(attempts) <= task["max_attempts"]
    running_runs = [run for run in detail["runs"] if run["status"] == "running"]
    assert len(running_runs) <= 1
    for run in detail["runs"]:
        if run["status"] == "failed":
            assert run["finished_at"] is not None
            assert run["error"]
        else:
            assert run["finished_at"] is None
    assert detail["attempt_count"] == len(detail["runs"])


def test_concurrent_cancel_and_dispatch_have_single_transition(
    client: TestClient,
) -> None:
    create_dataset_and_version(client)
    task = make_task(client, "flaky", max_attempts=2)
    run = run_task(client, task["id"])
    cancel_url = f"{TASKS_PATH}/{task['id']}/runs/{run['id']}/cancel"

    barrier = threading.Barrier(2)
    outcomes: dict[str, int] = {}

    def canceller() -> None:
        thread_client = TestClient(client.app)
        barrier.wait()
        response = thread_client.post(cancel_url, json={"reason": "stop"})
        outcomes["cancel"] = response.status_code

    def dispatcher() -> None:
        thread_client = TestClient(client.app)
        barrier.wait()
        response = thread_client.post(DISPATCH_PATH, json={"limit": 10})
        outcomes["dispatch"] = response.status_code
        outcomes["dispatch_runs"] = len(response.json()["runs"])

    threads = [threading.Thread(target=canceller), threading.Thread(target=dispatcher)]
    for thread in threads:
        thread.start()
    for thread in threads:
        thread.join()

    # While the run is 'running' dispatch cannot touch the task; once the
    # cancel commits, dispatch may claim the remaining attempt. Either way the
    # two operations never both transition the running run.
    detail = task_detail(client, task["id"])
    assert len(detail["runs"]) <= 2
    attempts = [r["attempt"] for r in detail["runs"]]
    assert attempts == list(range(1, len(attempts) + 1))
    assert len([r for r in detail["runs"] if r["status"] == "running"]) <= 1
    assert detail["runs"][0]["status"] == "failed"
    assert detail["runs"][0]["finished_at"] is not None
    assert detail["attempt_count"] == len(detail["runs"])

def _run_script(db_path: Path, script: str) -> str:
    env = os.environ.copy()
    env["DATA_LINEAGE_DB"] = str(db_path)
    result = subprocess.run(
        [sys.executable, "-c", script],
        cwd=PROJECT_ROOT,
        env=env,
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
    )
    assert result.returncode == 0, result.stderr
    return result.stdout.strip()

457	CREATE_SCRIPT = """
458	from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
459	from app.main import app
460	
461	client = TestClient(app)
462	
463	def ok(response, status=201):
464	    assert response.status_code == status, response.text
465	    return response.json()
466	
467	ok(client.post("/datasets", json={"name": "orders"}))
468	ok(client.post(
469	    "/datasets/orders/versions",
470	    json={"fields": [{"name": "id", "type": "integer", "nullable": False}]},
471	))
472	base = "/datasets/orders/versions/1/processing-tasks"
473	extract = ok(client.post(base, json={"name": "extract", "max_attempts": 2}))
474	load = ok(client.post(base, json={"name": "load", "depends_on": [extract["id"]]}))
475	run = ok(client.post(f"{base}/{extract['id']}/runs"))
476	ok(client.patch(
477	    f"{base}/{extract['id']}/runs/{run['id']}", json={"status": "succeeded"}
478	), status=200)
479	print("created")
480	"""
481	
482	VERIFY_SCRIPT = """
483	from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
484	from app.main import app
485	
486	client = TestClient(app)
487	base = "/datasets/orders/versions/1/processing-tasks"
488	
489	tasks = client.get(base)
490	assert tasks.status_code == 200, tasks.text
491	by_name = {task["name"]: task for task in tasks.json()}
492	assert set(by_name) == {"extract", "load"}
493	extract = by_name["extract"]
494	assert extract["status"] == "succeeded"
495	assert extract["attempt_count"] == 1
496	assert extract["max_attempts"] == 2
497	assert by_name["load"]["depends_on"] == [extract["id"]]
498	assert by_name["load"]["status"] == "pending"
499	
500	detail = client.get(f"{base}/{extract['id']}")
501	assert detail.status_code == 200, detail.text
502	runs = detail.json()["runs"]
503	assert len(runs) == 1
504	assert runs[0]["status"] == "succeeded"
505	assert runs[0]["finished_at"] is not None
506	
507	# The dependency is satisfied after the restart, so 'load' can start.
508	started = client.post(f"{base}/{by_name['load']['id']}/runs")
509	assert started.status_code == 201, started.text
510	assert started.json()["status"] == "running"
511	print("verified")
512	"""
513	
514	
515	def _run_script(db_path: Path, script: str) -> str:
516	    env = os.environ.copy()
517	    env["DATA_LINEAGE_DB"] = str(db_path)
518	    result = subprocess.run(
519	        [sys.executable, "-c", script],
520	        cwd=PROJECT_ROOT,
521	        env=env,
522	        capture_output=True,
523	        text=True,
524	    )
525	    assert result.returncode == 0, result.stderr
526	    return result.stdout.strip()
527	
528	
529	def test_tasks_and_runs_survive_process_restart(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
530	    db_path = tmp_path / "persisted-tasks.db"
531	    assert _run_script(db_path, CREATE_SCRIPT) == "created"
532	    assert db_path.exists()
533	    assert _run_script(db_path, VERIFY_SCRIPT) == "verified"

"""Tests for persistent processing tasks and their runs."""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
from datetime import datetime
from pathlib import Path

from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

PROJECT_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]

TASKS_PATH = "/datasets/orders/versions/1/processing-tasks"


def create_dataset_and_version(client: TestClient, dataset: str = "orders") -> None:
    response = client.post("/datasets", json={"name": dataset})
    assert response.status_code == 201, response.text
    response = client.post(
        f"/datasets/{dataset}/versions",
        json={"fields": [{"name": "id", "type": "integer", "nullable": False}]},
    )
    assert response.status_code == 201, response.text


def make_task(client: TestClient, name: str, **overrides):
    body = {"name": name, **overrides}
    response = client.post(TASKS_PATH, json=body)
    assert response.status_code == 201, response.text
    return response.json()

load = ok(client.post(base, json={"name": "load", "depends_on": [extract["id"]]}))

assert len(runs) == 1

# The dependency is satisfied after the restart, so 'load' can start.
started = client.post(f"{base}/{by_name['load']['id']}/runs")

def _run_script(db_path: Path, script: str) -> str:
    env = os.environ.copy()
    env["DATA_LINEAGE_DB"] = str(db_path)
    result = subprocess.run(
        [sys.executable, "-c", script],
        cwd=PROJECT_ROOT,
        env=env,
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
    )
    assert result.returncode == 0, result.stderr
    return result.stdout.strip()


def test_tasks_and_runs_survive_process_restart(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    db_path = tmp_path / "persisted-tasks.db"
    assert _run_script(db_path, CREATE_SCRIPT) == "created"
    assert db_path.exists()
    assert _run_script(db_path, VERIFY_SCRIPT) == "verified"

"""Tests for dependency-graph editing (PUT .../dependencies) and the schedule
view (GET .../processing-tasks/schedule)."""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

PROJECT_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]

BASE = "/datasets/orders/versions/1/processing-tasks"

TASK_FIELDS = {
    "id",
    "dataset",
    "version",
    "name",
    "depends_on",
    "max_attempts",
    "status",
    "attempt_count",
    "created_at",
}


def setup(client: TestClient, dataset: str = "orders", version: int = 1) -> None:
    response = client.post("/datasets", json={"name": dataset})
    assert response.status_code == 201, response.text
    response = client.post(
        f"/datasets/{dataset}/versions",
        json={"fields": [{"name": "id", "type": "integer", "nullable": False}]},
    )
    assert response.status_code == 201, response.text
    for extra in range(2, version + 1):
        response = client.post(
            f"/datasets/{dataset}/versions",
            json={"fields": [{"name": "id", "type": "integer", "nullable": False}]},
        )
        assert response.status_code == 201, response.text


def make_task(client: TestClient, name: str, **overrides) -> dict:
    response = client.post(BASE, json={"name": name, **overrides})
    assert response.status_code == 201, response.text
    return response.json()


def run_task(client: TestClient, task_id: int) -> dict:

def _run_script(db_path: Path, script: str) -> str:
    env = os.environ.copy()
    env["DATA_LINEAGE_DB"] = str(db_path)
    result = subprocess.run(
        [sys.executable, "-c", script],
        cwd=PROJECT_ROOT,
        env=env,
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
    )
    assert result.returncode == 0, result.stderr
    return result.stdout.strip()


def test_dependencies_and_schedule_survive_process_restart(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    db_path = tmp_path / "persisted-schedule.db"
    assert _run_script(db_path, CREATE_SCRIPT) == "created"
    assert db_path.exists()
    assert _run_script(db_path, VERIFY_SCRIPT) == "verified"

def batch_complete_task_runs(
    conn: sqlite3.Connection,
    dataset_name: str,
    version_number: int,
    items: list[dict[str, Any]],
    *,
    query_keys: tuple[str, ...] = (),
) -> dict:
    """Complete many current runs of one version in a single transaction.

    Every item names a task of this version, one of its runs and the desired
    terminal status (``succeeded`` without an error, or ``failed`` with a
    non-empty trimmed error). The whole batch is validated before any row is
    written: an unknown path dataset/version, an item task outside the version
    or an unknown run is a 404; a run that exists in the same dataset and
    version but belongs to another item's task is a 422 (as are malformed
    status/error combinations, duplicate tasks and any query parameter); an
    already-ended run or a task that is not currently ``running`` is a 409.
    Any failure rolls the entire batch back, leaving statuses, timestamps and
    attempt counters untouched.

    The writes run under the processing write lock and ``BEGIN IMMEDIATE`` and
    use the same conditional ``UPDATE ... WHERE status = 'running'`` as the
    single-run finish/cancel, so a concurrent single finish, cancel or
    dispatch has a single winner; losers get a 409 with no half-written run.
    Tasks completing successfully in this same batch are visible to later
    scheduling reads (dependencies succeeded, no extra run or attempt).
    """
    with _processing_write_section():
        conn.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
        try:
            dataset = require_dataset(conn, dataset_name)
            version_row = _require_schema_version(conn, dataset, version_number)

            # Request-shape checks that are independent of the referenced rows.
            if query_keys:
                raise RequestInvalidError(
                    "The batch-complete endpoint does not accept query parameters"
                )

            seen_task_ids: set[int] = set()
            normalized: list[tuple[int, int, str, str | None]] = []
            for item in items:
                task_id = item["task_id"]
                run_id = item["run_id"]
                status = item["status"]
                error = item["error"]
                if task_id in seen_task_ids:
                    raise ConflictError(
                        f"Processing task {task_id} appears more than once in the "
                        "batch; each task may be completed at most once"
                    )
                seen_task_ids.add(task_id)
                if status == "succeeded":
                    if error is not None:
                        raise RequestInvalidError(
                            "A successful run must not carry an error message"
                        )
                    stored_error: str | None = None
                else:
                    if error is None or not error.strip():
                        raise RequestInvalidError(
                            "A failed run requires a non-empty error message"
                        )
                    stored_error = error.strip()
                normalized.append((task_id, run_id, status, stored_error))

            # Resolve and validate every item against the current committed
            # state before writing anything.
            resolved: list[tuple[sqlite3.Row, sqlite3.Row, str, str | None]] = []
            for task_id, run_id, status, stored_error in normalized:
                task_row = _require_task(
                    conn, version_row, dataset_name, version_number, task_id
                )
                run_row = conn.execute(
                    "SELECT * FROM processing_task_runs WHERE id = ?", (run_id,)
                ).fetchone()
                if run_row is None:
                    raise NotFoundError(
                        f"Processing task run {run_id} does not exist"
                    )
                if run_row["task_id"] != task_row["id"]:
                    # The run exists (possibly in another version): mismatched
                    # ownership is a malformed reference, not a missing one.
                    raise RequestInvalidError(
                        f"Processing task run {run_id} does not belong to task "
                        f"{task_id} in version {version_number} of dataset "
                        f"'{dataset_name}'"
                    )
                if task_row["status"] != "running":
                    raise ConflictError(
                        f"Processing task {task_id} is '{task_row['status']}' and "
                        "cannot be completed"
                    )
                if run_row["status"] != "running":
                    raise ConflictError(
                        f"Processing task run {run_id} is already "
                        f"'{run_row['status']}' and cannot be finished again"
                    )
                resolved.append((task_row, run_row, status, stored_error))

            finished_at = utc_now_iso()
            completed: list[dict] = []
            for task_row, run_row, status, stored_error in resolved:
                # The conditional write is the hard guard against a concurrent
                # finish/cancel: it matches only while the run is still
                # 'running', so a batch racing another writer either claims
                # every run or rolls the whole batch back with a 409.
                cursor = conn.execute(
                    "UPDATE processing_task_runs SET status = ?, finished_at = ?, "
                    "error = ? WHERE id = ? AND status = 'running'",
                    (status, finished_at, stored_error, run_row["id"]),
                )
                if cursor.rowcount != 1:
                    raise ConflictError(
                        f"Processing task run {run_row['id']} was finished concurrently"
                    )
                conn.execute(
                    "UPDATE processing_tasks SET status = ? WHERE id = ?",
                    (status, task_row["id"]),
                )
                updated = conn.execute(
                    "SELECT * FROM processing_task_runs WHERE id = ?", (run_row["id"],)
                ).fetchone()
                completed.append(_run_row_to_dict(updated))
        except BaseException:
            conn.rollback()
            raise

    completed.sort(key=lambda run: run["task_id"])
    return {
        "dataset": dataset["name"],
        "version": version_row["version"],
        "runs": completed,
    }

def batch_complete_task_runs(
    conn: sqlite3.Connection,
    dataset_name: str,
    version_number: int,
    items: list[dict[str, Any]],
    *,
    query_keys: tuple[str, ...] = (),
) -> dict:
    """Complete many current runs of one version in a single transaction.

    Every item names a task of this version, one of its runs and the desired
    terminal status (``succeeded`` without an error, or ``failed`` with a
    non-empty trimmed error). The whole batch is validated before any row is
    written: an unknown path dataset/version, an item task outside the version
    or an unknown run is a 404; a run that exists in the same dataset and
    version but belongs to another item's task is a 422 (as are malformed
    status/error combinations, duplicate tasks and any query parameter); an
    already-ended run or a task that is not currently ``running`` is a 409.
    Any failure rolls the entire batch back, leaving statuses, timestamps and
    attempt counters untouched.

    The writes run under the processing write lock and ``BEGIN IMMEDIATE`` and
    use the same conditional ``UPDATE ... WHERE status = 'running'`` as the
    single-run finish/cancel, so a concurrent single finish, cancel or
    dispatch has a single winner; losers get a 409 with no half-written run.
    Tasks completing successfully in this same batch are visible to later
    scheduling reads (dependencies succeeded, no extra run or attempt).
    """
    with _processing_write_section():
        conn.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
        try:
            dataset = require_dataset(conn, dataset_name)
            version_row = _require_schema_version(conn, dataset, version_number)

            # Request-shape checks that are independent of the referenced rows.
            if query_keys:
                raise RequestInvalidError(
                    "The batch-complete endpoint does not accept query parameters"
                )

            seen_task_ids: set[int] = set()
            normalized: list[tuple[int, int, str, str | None]] = []
            for item in items:
                task_id = item["task_id"]
                run_id = item["run_id"]
                status = item["status"]
                error = item["error"]
                if task_id in seen_task_ids:
                    raise ConflictError(
                        f"Processing task {task_id} appears more than once in the "
                        "batch; each task may be completed at most once"
                    )
                seen_task_ids.add(task_id)
                if status == "succeeded":
                    if error is not None:
                        raise RequestInvalidError(
                            "A successful run must not carry an error message"
                        )
                    stored_error: str | None = None
                else:
                    if error is None or not error.strip():
                        raise RequestInvalidError(
                            "A failed run requires a non-empty error message"
                        )
                    stored_error = error.strip()
                normalized.append((task_id, run_id, status, stored_error))

            # Resolve and validate every item against the current committed
            # state before writing anything.
            resolved: list[tuple[sqlite3.Row, sqlite3.Row, str, str | None]] = []
            for task_id, run_id, status, stored_error in normalized:
                task_row = _require_task(
                    conn, version_row, dataset_name, version_number, task_id
                )
                run_row = conn.execute(
                    "SELECT * FROM processing_task_runs WHERE id = ?", (run_id,)
                ).fetchone()
                if run_row is None:
                    raise NotFoundError(
                        f"Processing task run {run_id} does not exist"
                    )
                if run_row["task_id"] != task_row["id"]:
                    # The run exists (possibly in another version): mismatched
                    # ownership is a malformed reference, not a missing one.
                    raise RequestInvalidError(
                        f"Processing task run {run_id} does not belong to task "
                        f"{task_id} in version {version_number} of dataset "
                        f"'{dataset_name}'"
                    )
                if task_row["status"] != "running":
                    raise ConflictError(
                        f"Processing task {task_id} is '{task_row['status']}' and "
                        "cannot be completed"
                    )
                if run_row["status"] != "running":
                    raise ConflictError(
                        f"Processing task run {run_id} is already "
                        f"'{run_row['status']}' and cannot be finished again"
                    )
                resolved.append((task_row, run_row, status, stored_error))

            finished_at = utc_now_iso()
            completed: list[dict] = []
            for task_row, run_row, status, stored_error in resolved:
                # The conditional write is the hard guard against a concurrent
                # finish/cancel: it matches only while the run is still
                # 'running', so a batch racing another writer either claims
                # every run or rolls the whole batch back with a 409.
                cursor = conn.execute(
                    "UPDATE processing_task_runs SET status = ?, finished_at = ?, "
                    "error = ? WHERE id = ? AND status = 'running'",
                    (status, finished_at, stored_error, run_row["id"]),
                )
                if cursor.rowcount != 1:
                    raise ConflictError(
                        f"Processing task run {run_row['id']} was finished concurrently"
                    )
                conn.execute(
                    "UPDATE processing_tasks SET status = ? WHERE id = ?",
                    (status, task_row["id"]),
                )
                updated = conn.execute(
                    "SELECT * FROM processing_task_runs WHERE id = ?", (run_row["id"],)
                ).fetchone()
                completed.append(_run_row_to_dict(updated))
        except BaseException:
            conn.rollback()
            raise

    completed.sort(key=lambda run: run["task_id"])
    return {
        "dataset": dataset["name"],
        "version": version_row["version"],
        "runs": completed,
    }
